href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superuser\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003esuperuser\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eACL without users\u003c/strong\u003e: especially useful for systems that don't have authentication or user log-ins.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eACL without resources\u003c/strong\u003e: some scenarios may target for a type of resources instead of an individual resource by using permissions like \u003ccode\u003ewrite-article\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eread-log\u003c/code\u003e. It doesn't control the access to a specific article or log.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role-based_access_control\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eRBAC (Role-Based Access Control)\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRBAC with resource roles\u003c/strong\u003e: both users and resources can have roles (or groups) at the same time.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRBAC with domains/tenants\u003c/strong\u003e: users can have different role sets for different domains/tenants.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attribute-Based_Access_Control\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control)\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e: syntax sugar like \u003ccode\u003eresource.Owner\u003c/code\u003e can be used to get the attribute for a resource.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eRESTful\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e: supports paths like \u003ccode\u003e/res/*\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e/res/:id\u003c/code\u003e and HTTP methods like \u003ccode\u003eGET\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ePOST\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ePUT\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eDELETE\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDeny-override\u003c/strong\u003e: CONF file based on the \u003cstrong\u003ePERM metamodel (Policy, Effect, Request, Matchers)\u003c/strong\u003e. So switching or upgrading the authorization mechanism for a project is just as simple as modifying a configuration. You can customize your own access control model by combining the available models. For example, you can get RBAC roles and ABAC attributes together inside one model and share one set of policy rules.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe most basic and simplest model in Casbin is ACL. Matchers\n[matchers]\nm = r.sub == p.sub \u0026amp;\u0026amp; r.obj == p.obj \u0026amp;\u0026amp; r.act == p.act\n\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan does:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eenforce the policy in the classic \u003ccode\u003e{subject, object, action}\u003c/code\u003e form or a customized form as you defined, both allow and deny authorizations are supported.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ehandle the storage of the access control model and its policy.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003emanage the role-user mappings and role-role mappings (aka role hierarchy in RBAC).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003esupport built-in superuser like \u003ccode\u003eroot\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eadministrator\u003c/code\u003e. A superuser can do anything without explicit permissions.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003emultiple built-in operators to support the rule matching. For example, \u003ccode\u003ekeyMatch\u003c/code\u003e can map a resource key \u003ccode\u003e/foo/bar\u003c/code\u003e to the pattern \u003ccode\u003e/foo*\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhat Apache Casbin does NOT do:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eauthentication (aka verify \u003ccode\u003eusername\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003epassword\u003c/code\u003e when a user logs in)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003emanage the list of users or roles. I believe it's more convenient for the project itself to manage these entities. Users usually have their passwords, and Apache Casbin is not designed as a password container. However, Apache Casbin stores the user-role mapping for the RBAC scenario.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" <h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Supported models</h2>
<a id="user-content-supported-models" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Supported models" href="#supported-models">
<svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true">
<path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path>
</svg>
</a>

<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_control_list" rel="nofollow">
<strong>ACL (Access Control List)</strong>
</a>
</li>
<li>
<strong>
ACL with 
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superuser" rel="nofollow">superuser</a>
</strong>
</li>
<li>
<strong>ACL without users</strong>
: especially useful for systems that don't have authentication or user log-ins.
</li>
<li>
<strong>ACL without resources</strong>
: some scenarios may target for a type of resources instead of an individual resource by using permissions like 
<code>write-article</code>
, 
<code>read-log</code>
. It doesn't control the access to a specific article or log.
</li>
<li>
<strong>
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role-based_access_control" rel="nofollow">RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)</a>
</strong>
</li>
<li>
<strong>RBAC with resource roles</strong>
: both users and resources can have roles (or groups) at the same time.
</li>
<li>
<strong>RBAC with domains/tenants</strong>
: users can have different role sets for different domains/tenants.
</li>
<li>
<strong>
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attribute-Based_Access_Control" rel="nofollow">ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control)</a>
</strong>
: syntax sugar like 
<code>resource.Owner</code>
 can be used to get the attribute for a resource.
</li>
<li>
<strong>
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer" rel="nofollow">RESTful</a>
</strong>
: supports paths like 
<code>/res/*</code>
, 
<code>/res/:id</code>
 and HTTP methods like 
<code>GET</code>
, 
<code>POST</code>
, 
<code>PUT</code>
, 
<code>DELETE</code>
.
</li>
<li>
<strong>Deny-override</strong>
: both allow and deny authorizations are supported, deny overrides the allow.
</li>
<li>
<strong>Priority</strong>
: the policy rules can be prioritized like firewall rules.
</li>
</ol>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">
<h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How it works?</h2>
<a id="user-content-how-it-works" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How it works?" href="#how-it-works">
<svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true">
<path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path>
</svg>
</a>

<p dir="auto">
In Casbin, an access control model is abstracted into a CONF file based on the 
<strong>PERM metamodel (Policy, Effect, Request, Matchers)</strong>
. So switching or upgrading the authorization mechanism for a project is just as simple as modifying a configuration. You can customize your own access control model by combining the available models. For example, you can get RBAC roles and ABAC attributes together inside one model and share one set of policy rules.
</p>
<p dir="auto">The most basic and simplest model in Casbin is ACL. ACL's model CONF is:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-ini notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-c">
<span class="pl-c">#</span>
 Request definition
</span>
<span class="pl-en">[request_definition]</span>
<span class="pl-k">r</span>
 = sub, obj, act


<span class="pl-c">
<span class="pl-c">#</span>
 Policy definition
</span>
<span class="pl-en">[policy_definition]</span>
<span class="pl-k">p</span>
 = sub, obj, act


<span class="pl-c">
<span class="pl-c">#</span>
 Policy effect
</span>
<span class="pl-en">[policy_effect]</span>
<span class="pl-k">e</span>
 = some(where (
<span class="pl-k">p.eft</span>
 == allow))


<span class="pl-c">
<span class="pl-c">#</span>
 Matchers
</span>
<span class="pl-en">[matchers]</span>
<span class="pl-k">m</span>
 = 
<span class="pl-k">r.sub</span>
 == p.sub && 
<span class="pl-k">r.obj</span>
 == p.obj && 
<span class="pl-k">r.act</span>
 == p.act

</pre>
<div class="zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center" data-copy-feedback="Copied!" data-tooltip-direction="w" value="# Request definition
[request_definition]

# Policy definition
[policy_definition]

# Policy effect
[policy_effect]
e = some(where (p.eft == allow))

# Matchers
[matchers]
m = r.sub == p.sub && r.obj == p.obj && r.act == p.act
" tabindex="0" role="button">

<p dir="auto">It means:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
alice can read data1

<li>

<p dir="auto">We also support multi-line mode by appending '\'  in the end:</p>

</span>

 = 
<span class="pl-k">r.sub</span>
 == p.sub && 
<span class="pl-k">r.obj</span>
 == p.obj \
  && 
<span class="pl-k">r.act</span>
 == p.act
</pre>

<p dir="auto">
Further more, if you are using ABAC,  you can try operator 
<code>in</code>
 like following in Casbin 
<strong>golang</strong>
 edition (jCasbin and Node-Casbin are not supported yet):
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-ini notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-c">
<span class="pl-c">#</span>
 Matchers
</span>
<span class="pl-en">[matchers]</span>
<span class="pl-k">m</span>
 = 
<span class="pl-k">r.obj</span>
 == p.obj && 
<span class="pl-k">r.act</span>
 == p.act || r.obj in (
<span class="pl-s">
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
data2
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
data3
<span class="pl-pds">'</span>
</span>
)
</pre>

</a>
</div>
<p dir="auto">What Apache Casbin does:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
enforce the policy in the classic 
<code>{subject, object, action}</code>
 form or a customized form as you defined, both allow and deny authorizations are supported.
</li>
<li>
handle the storage of the access control model and its policy.
</li>
<li>
manage the role-user mappings and role-role mappings (aka role hierarchy in RBAC).
</li>
<li>
support built-in superuser like 
<code>root</code>
 or 
<code>administrator</code>
. A superuser can do anything without explicit permissions.
</li>
<li>
multiple built-in operators to support the rule matching. For example, 
<code>keyMatch</code>
 can map a resource key 
<code>/foo/bar</code>
 to the pattern 
<code>/foo*</code>
.
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">What Apache Casbin does NOT do:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
authentication (aka verify 
<code>username</code>
 and 
<code>password</code>
 when a user logs in)
</li>
<li>
manage the list of users or roles. I believe it's more convenient for the project itself to manage these entities. Users usually have their passwords, and Apache Casbin is not designed as a password container. However, Apache Casbin stores the user-role mapping for the RBAC scenario.
</li>
</ol>

<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">New a Casbin enforcer with a model file and a policy file:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-go notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-s1">e</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">_</span> <span class="pl-c1">:=</span> <span class="pl-s1">casbin</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">NewEnforcer</span>
(
<span class="pl-s">"path/to/model.conf"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"path/to/policy.csv"</span>
)
</pre>

<p dir="auto">Add an enforcement hook into your code right before the access happens:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-go notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-s1">sub</span> <span class="pl-c1">:=</span> <span class="pl-s">"alice"</span> <span class="pl-c">// the user that wants to access a resource.</span>
<span class="pl-s1">obj</span> <span class="pl-c1">:=</span> <span class="pl-s">"data1"</span> <span class="pl-c">// the resource that is going to be accessed.</span>
<span class="pl-s1">act</span> <span class="pl-c1">:=</span> <span class="pl-s">"read"</span> <span class="pl-c">// the operation that the user performs on the resource.</span>

<span class="pl-k">if</span> <span class="pl-s1">res</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">_</span> <span class="pl-c1">:=</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">Enforce</span>
(
<span class="pl-s1">sub</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">obj</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">act</span>
); 
<span class="pl-s1">res</span>
 {
    
<span class="pl-c">// permit alice to read data1</span>

} 
<span class="pl-k">else</span>
 {
    
<span class="pl-c">// deny the request, show an error</span>

}
</pre>

<p dir="auto">Apache Casbin provides two sets of APIs to manage permissions:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<a href="https://casbin.apache.org/docs/management-api" rel="nofollow">Management API</a>
: the primitive API that provides full support for Apache Casbin policy management.
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://casbin.apache.org/docs/rbac-api" rel="nofollow">RBAC API</a>
: a more friendly API for RBAC. This API is a subset of Management API. The RBAC users could use this API to simplify the code.
</li>
</ul>
